headline: Gen X creators are winning fans on TikTok

sources.title: Are my gen X peers the influencers the world has been waiting for? (The Guardian)
This Gen Xer spent 28 years in a cubicle and never made more than $70,000. At 59, she made $500,000 in the creator economy (Fortune)
Overlooked and Under-Marketed: "Gen X" Emerges as Most Influential Global Consumer Cohort, According to NIQ and World Data Lab (NIQ)

chunks.text: On October 4, 2026, a British writer published an [[opinion column]] in the Guardian about her generation. She is 51 and part of Generation X, people born between 1965 and 1980. She said a [[marketing expert]] on TikTok had told viewers to stop {{sleeping on}} Gen X. In his view, Gen X has become a strong but [[underrated]] force online. She asked whether her [[peers]] could {{take over}} as the next big influencers.

verbs.correct: To fail to see how good someone is
verbs.wrong: To pay someone to post an ad
verbs.why: Critics slept on the movie when it first came out. Don't sleep on our goalie, because she is very good. A marketing expert on TikTok told viewers to stop sleeping on Gen X.

verbs.wrong: To leave a job for a new one
verbs.why: Who will take over as captain next year? She took over as manager when her boss retired. The writer asked whether her Gen X peers could take over as the next big influencers.

chunks.text: Gen X has a lot of [[buying power]]. A [[market research]] company reported in July 2025 that Gen X became the world's top-spending generation in 2021. Gen X women [[influence]] 70 to 80 percent of [[household]] buying decisions. According to the column, many young people now think Gen X is cool. But the writer says her generation is not known for {{showing off}}. Many of them are busy {{looking after}} [[aging parents]] and worried children.

verbs.correct: To try to make people admire you
verbs.wrong: To post the same video twice
verbs.why: He likes to show off his new car. Stop showing off and just play the game. The writer says her generation is not known for showing off.

verbs.correct: To keep someone safe and well
verbs.wrong: To give someone a new name
verbs.why: I look after my sister's dog on the weekend. Nurses look after patients day and night. Many Gen Xers are busy looking after aging parents and worried children.

chunks.text: The column's main example is a food director at a large British [[store chain]]. She {{set up}} her TikTok account in May 2026. Her videos have {{racked up}} as many as 2 million [[views]], and nearly 250,000 people follow her. She {{talks viewers through}} new food products. In the writer's view, she {{comes across as}} calm and [[competent]]. Many fans {{look up to}} her. One wrote that they would follow her into war.

verbs.wrong: To rate a post with stars
verbs.why: I set up a new email account last night. She set up a bank account for her son. The food director set up her TikTok account in May 2026.
Our team racked up ten wins in a row. She racked up a lot of miles on her old car. Her videos have racked up as many as 2 million views.

verbs.correct: To explain something step by step
verbs.wrong: To film a video in a store
verbs.why: The teacher talked us through the math problem. Can you talk me through the new phone app? In her videos, the food director talks viewers through new food products.

verbs.correct: To seem a certain way to others
verbs.why: He comes across as shy, but he is very funny. She came across as nervous in the interview. In the writer's view, the food director comes across as calm and competent.
Many kids look up to their older brothers and sisters. I always looked up to my grandfather. Many fans look up to the food director, and one wrote that they would follow her into war.

chunks.text: In August, the business magazine Fortune described a 59-year-old former [[insurance]] worker who {{brought in}} about 500,000 dollars in 2025 from online videos and sales. She says fears about being too old should not {{hold people back}}. A marketing professor in Germany told the magazine that brands have a [[blind spot]] for age. The Guardian writer loves seeing [[capable]] people like the food director {{popping up}} online. She hopes more of her peers will be less [[modest]] and [[shine]].

verbs.correct: To earn an amount of money
verbs.why: My summer job brings in about 300 dollars a week. The bake sale brought in 800 dollars for the school. The former insurance worker brought in about 500,000 dollars in 2025.
Don't let one bad grade hold you back. His fear of flying held him back at work. She says fears about being too old should not hold people back.
Ads keep popping up on my phone. New coffee shops are popping up all over town. The writer loves seeing capable people like the food director popping up online.

ex: The company hired a marketing expert to plan its ads.
A marketing expert said the logo was too busy.

wordDefs.def: Better or more important than most people think

wordDefs.def: People who are the same age or have the same position as you

wordDefs.def: Relating to a home and the people in it
ex: Our household bills went up this winter.
Washing the dishes is one of my household chores.

wordDefs.def: Mothers and fathers who are getting old and may need help
ex: Many adults spend weekends helping their aging parents.

Caring for aging parents can be hard on a family.

wordDefs.def: A group of stores with the same name and owner
ex: The store chain opened ten new shops this year.

wordDefs.def: The number of times people have watched a video

wordDefs.def: A plan where you pay a company to cover the cost if something bad happens
ex: Car insurance is required in most states.

wordDefs.def: Something a person or group does not notice or understand
ex: Money is a blind spot for many young couples.

ex: He is too modest to talk about his prize.

wordDefs.def: To do very well and be noticed for it
ex: The quiet student really shines in math class.

mainIdea.s: A columnist asks whether middle-aged Gen X adults could become the next big online influencers. Her main example is a capable food director whose TikTok videos now draw huge numbers of viewers.
mainIdea.why: The writer asks if her peers could take over as influencers. She points to a food director whose videos have racked up as many as 2 million views.

mainIdea.s: A Guardian writer says people her age are now the most popular creators on TikTok. She believes young viewers prefer them because Gen X adults love to share their success and spend freely.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the writer only asks whether Gen X could become big influencers. She also says her generation is not known for showing off.

mainIdea.s: A new study finds that adults born between 1965 and 1980 spend more hours on social media than teenagers do. Researchers say many of them check TikTok several times a day, mostly late at night.
mainIdea.why: This is a column asking if Gen X could become influencers. It uses a food director who set up a TikTok account in May as its example.

tf.s: A marketing expert told viewers to stop sleeping on Gen X.
tf.why: He said this on TikTok. In his view, Gen X has become a strong but underrated force online.

tf.s: The food director set up her TikTok account in 2020.
tf.why: She set up her TikTok account in May 2026, not in 2020.

tf.s: Her videos have racked up as many as 2 million views.
tf.why: Her videos have reached up to 2 million views, and nearly 250,000 people follow her.

tf.s: The writer says her generation is known for showing off.
tf.why: She says Gen X is not known for showing off. Many of them are busy looking after aging parents and worried children.

tf.s: The former insurance worker brought in about 50,000 dollars in 2025.
tf.why: She brought in about 500,000 dollars that year from making videos for brands and selling products online.

tf.s: Many fans look up to the food director at the store chain.
tf.why: Fans look up to her, and one wrote that they would follow her into war.

lines.text: Have you heard people saying "stop {{sleeping on}} Gen X"?
A marketing expert on TikTok says people in their forties, fifties and early sixties are a big force online. They just fly [[under the radar]].
A Guardian column described a food director at a big British store chain. She {{set up}} her TikTok account in May.
Her videos have {{racked up}} as many as two million views. She {{talks viewers through}} new food products.
That's the surprise. She {{comes across as}} calm and competent, and she really [[knows her stuff]].
So she's [[the real deal]], not someone selling a fake lifestyle.
Exactly. A lot of fans seem to {{look up to}} her.
Does the writer want more people her age to start posting?
Yes, but she admits it's hard. Many of them are busy {{looking after}} aging parents and kids.
And Gen X isn't known for {{showing off}}.
True. Still, Fortune wrote about a 59-year-old woman who {{brought in}} about 500,000 dollars last year.
She says fears about age shouldn't {{hold people back}}.
I like that. It's [[a breath of fresh air]] after so many young influencers.

expressions.def: Used to say that something is not noticed by most people
ex: The little cafe stayed under the radar for years.
Some great players fly under the radar.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone has real skill and knowledge in her job
ex: Ask the nurse. She really knows her stuff.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone is truly as good as they seem
ex: That new chef is the real deal.
After one song, we knew the band was the real deal.

expressions.def: A person who becomes successful later in life than most people
ex: My aunt was a late bloomer who started painting at 50.

expressions.def: Used to praise something new and different that feels pleasant
ex: Her honest speech was a breath of fresh air.
